statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of four public-news archetypes.

page.notes: Large Spanish-language news publication with server-rendered content, client hydration, advertising, consent, PWA manifest and service worker.

checkOutcomes.evidence: White surfaces remain unchanged under dark preference.
15 two-second skeleton animations remain active and no reduced-motion media rule was found.
The document permits UA forced-color adaptation (forced-color-adjust:auto) and advertises light/dark color scheme.
No view-transition treatment was present for route or state changes.
The 67,509 px feed has no scroll-timeline or progress treatment.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile screenshots, layout metrics and target inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Native vertical scrolling remains available without horizontal overflow; persistent mobile navigation targets are 42 px high.
A persistent bottom navigation keeps Home, Sections, Foodit, Club and Account available across tested templates.
Menus, consent dialog and bottom navigation are positioned relative to their intended viewport/component without clipping.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual hierarchy review across representative pages.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lead headline, section label and dollar data are visually prioritized above secondary cards once prompts are dismissed.
A viewport-filling consent dialog blocks each path; desktop also stacks a notification prompt.
The consent surface is exposed as role=dialog with a label, focus target and option controls.
Prompts, ad inventory and mixed modules dominate the opening and create a 67,509 px homepage.
All four layouts report scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 and horizontalOverflowPx=0.
Cards collapse to mobile columns and navigation changes to a bottom bar without clipping.
Primary mobile navigation targets are 42 px high and standard button/link semantics preserve keyboard and touch input.

checkOutcomes.method: Title, H1 and visual hierarchy review.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The publication purpose and lead story are explicit; article, section and dollar templates expose task-specific headings.

checkOutcomes.method: Fresh-session journey review across four archetypes.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Every primary path is initially blocked by consent.
Consent presents labeled choices and the dollar template exposes current values; standard page navigation remains available.
Lighthouse LCP 8.6 s, FCP 5.6 s and TBT 1,070 ms; trace LCP was 1.67 s unthrottled.

checkOutcomes.method: Layout observers on four mobile templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Observed CLS ranges 0.021–0.052 with no horizontal overflow, within the good threshold.
Lighthouse TBT is 1,070 ms and TTI 33.8 s; trace captured tasks up to 95 ms.
188 requests transfer 4.07 MB, including 2.82 MB script.
Multiple GTM/gtag and ad-tech scripts dominate transferred bytes.
A focusable Prode link and several visible controls have no discernible name.
Consent text ratios of 1.82:1 and 2.8:1 fail 4.5:1.
Pages use a single content H1 before section headings; the consent dialog is labeled and focusable.
Article and headline text remains readable and reflows at 360 px without clipping.
No horizontal overflow occurs and primary mobile navigation targets are 42 px high.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse console audit and HAR hygiene.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Normal load logs FedCM, CORS, network and 404 errors.
HTML doctype, UTF-8 charset, viewport metadata and canonical metadata are present; missing image dimensions are handled under performance/sustainability.
Deprecated Attribution Reporting use and an unload handler preventing bfcache were reported.
Home and article have descriptive titles and meta descriptions in raw HTML.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability pair, robots and mobile layout.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw HTML coverage is 96% home and 89% article; robots allows public content and four mobile templates have no overflow.
Canonical URLs, max-image-preview robots metadata and multiple declared sitemap indexes are present.
Home has three JSON-LD blocks and Open Graph metadata; article has five JSON-LD blocks and Open Graph metadata.
HTTPS is used, but HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
53 third-party origins, 14 known tracker domains, 134 third-party requests and insecure/long-lived cookies were observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual prompt and Lighthouse identity inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Notification permission is requested through an in-page prompt rather than immediate browser permission; sign-in is user initiated. No sensitive secrets were found.
CSP only declares frame-ancestors and other defensive policies are absent.
Core content is server-rendered: 96% home and 89% article token coverage without JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse and HAR runtime error review.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Optional identity/ad integrations emit multiple errors during normal load.
A standalone manifest with icons/screenshots and an active service worker registration are present.
Fresh Cache Storage is empty and a missing route returns an unadorned 404 response.
The document declares lang=es; Spanish content and responsive layouts render in the expected left-to-right direction.
Argentine peso/dollar values, decimal commas and Spanish labels are localized consistently on home and dollar paths.

checkOutcomes.method: Article metadata and visible publication context review.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Article publication/current-market context is presented consistently for the Argentine edition without contradictory timezone rendering.
The first layer offers Accept and Manage but no equally direct Reject all while blocking content.
No user-entered form error is shown on the audited public paths; consent controls use plain Spanish labels and remain reversible through management.

checkOutcomes.method: Form inventory across audited public paths.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No user data-entry form is present on the home/article/section/dollar templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user data-entry form exists on the representative public-news templates; authenticated account and checkout are on separate domains and outside scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Subscription price and account links are visibly labeled; no checkout was entered because it leaves the audited origin.
93 images lack dimensions, 87 lack srcset and 93 use legacy formats.
4.07 MB/188 requests load initially and 15 skeleton animations continue under reduced motion.
Third parties account for 2.90 MB and 134 requests.
This is a public editorial reading surface, not an agent-operable application; discoverability is covered separately.
checkOutcomes.reason: No transaction or tool-like capability on the audited public-news templates requires WebMCP/agent action exposure.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarization or local-AI feature is offered or required for the core reading task.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative news-reading experience has no user-facing inference feature for which on-device execution is applicable.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/post heap summaries around ten scroll cycles.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Separate fresh runs show a modest 2.4 MB (3%) difference with no Detached constructor among top retained types; this does not establish a leak.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary and DOM/network scale review.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline has 1.32 million nodes and 79.3 MB self size, high for an initial news page.
No Detached DOM constructor appears among top retained constructors after repeated scrolling; object growth is modest and non-diagnostic.

principleOutcomes.reason: No transaction or tool-like capability on the audited public-news templates requires WebMCP/agent action exposure. The representative news-reading experience has no user-facing inference feature for which on-device execution is applicable.

paths.description: Homepage and lead-news feed: represents primary discovery, global navigation, consent, advertising and performance.
Lead politics article: represents editorial detail, reading, metadata and crawler visibility.
El Mundo section: represents a category/listing template.
Dólar Hoy: represents a high-value live-data utility template.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt its surfaces to a dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: white content and consent surfaces remain unchanged under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-aware surface, text, border, image and embedded-widget colors, using light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme layer.

findings.summary: Loading animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found 15 running skeleton animations, each with a 2000 ms duration, and zero accessible prefers-reduced-motion rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential skeleton and transition motion inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce while preserving immediate state feedback.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use coherent view transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection and the active-animation probe found loading animations but no same-document or cross-document view-transition treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use progressive-enhancement View Transitions for article/list navigation where it improves spatial continuity, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The long feed has no scroll-linked progress or spatial feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 67,509 CSS pixels tall, while DOM and animation inspection found no scroll-timeline progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained scroll-driven reading/progress affordance for long pages; avoid decorative motion and respect reduced motion.

findings.summary: Consent and notification prompts obscure the primary news content on every tested archetype.
findings.evidence: Desktop and all three mobile archetype screenshots open with a full blocking consent dialog; desktop also shows a notification prompt behind it.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer the notification request until intent is shown and redesign consent so essential content remains available with equally clear accept/reject choices.

findings.summary: Advertising, prompts and a very long mixed-content feed compete with the primary news task.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 67,509 CSS pixels tall and the initial desktop view contains ad space, two stacked prompts, market tickers and subscription chrome before readers can engage.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce simultaneous chrome, reserve a calm content-first opening, and progressively disclose secondary modules.

findings.summary: Reading is interrupted before the primary flow can begin.
findings.evidence: Fresh sessions on home, article, section and dollar pages all show the same viewport-filling consent dialog before the underlying task is usable.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep reading available while consent is decided, and provide direct, symmetric controls for accept, reject and preference management.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is poor despite acceptable visual stability.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.6 s, FCP 5.6 s, TBT 1,070 ms and performance 0.33; the independent trace measured LCP 1.67 s in an unthrottled run, confirming strong condition sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP chain under mobile throttling, prioritize only the LCP resource and critical CSS, then remove or delay non-critical script work.

findings.summary: Main-thread work delays interactivity.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 1,070 ms total blocking time and 33.8 s time to interactive; the raw trace also captured long tasks up to 95 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, schedule non-urgent work after interaction readiness, and defer analytics/ad initialization until consent and idle time.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers a large, script-heavy payload.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 188 requests and 4.07 MB transferred; scripts account for 2.82 MB, with 134 third-party requests transferring 2.90 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level request/byte budget, remove duplicate tags, self-host or consolidate critical assets, and lazy-load media and commercial modules.

findings.summary: Third-party and duplicated tag code dominates the payload.
findings.evidence: Five Google Tag Manager/gtag resources and multiple ad/analytics vendors appear among the largest scripts; third parties contribute 71% of transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit tag ownership and coverage, eliminate duplicate destinations, and load optional vendors only after purpose-specific consent.

findings.summary: Some interactive controls and links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name for a focusable Prode link; the custom probe also found multiple visible links and buttons with empty accessible names.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every focusable icon, image link and custom component a stable accessible name; remove hidden empty links from the tab order.

findings.summary: Consent dialog text fails contrast requirements.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 1.82:1 for “Más información” and 2.8:1 for “Lista de partners”, below the required 4.5:1 for 12 px normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use opaque dialog surfaces and text colors that maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast in default and overlay states.

findings.summary: Production loads emit console and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured FedCM errors, a CORS-blocked ad-tech request, a failed resource and a 404 control-group endpoint.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or guard failing integrations, handle expected identity states without console errors, and monitor first-party 4xx/CORS regressions.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and an unload handler reduce browser compatibility and navigation performance.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported an Attribution Reporting deprecation and an unload handler that prevents back/forward cache restoration.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload handlers in favor of pagehide/visibilitychange and update the responsible third-party integration away from deprecated APIs.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but important transport and response protections are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. CSP only contains frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and nosniff; deploy a restrictive CSP beyond frame-ancestors; set explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The page exposes readers to an unusually broad tracking and advertising surface.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 53 third-party origins and 14 known tracker domains; HAR attributes 134 requests and 2.90 MB to third parties. Thirteen cookies were set and several analytics cookies were insecure or long-lived.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors and purposes, block optional requests before consent, shorten retention, and set Secure/SameSite attributes consistently.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The only CSP directive observed is frame-ancestors; Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy, nosniff and HSTS are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out nonce/hash-based script-src and restrictive default-src/object-src/base-uri directives, plus explicit permissions and referrer policies.

findings.summary: Third-party failures leak into the production runtime.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse logged identity, CORS, network and 404 errors during a normal load instead of isolating optional integrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Contain optional integrations behind timeouts/error boundaries and ensure failures cannot affect navigation, reading or consent controls.

findings.summary: The installable surface has no observable cached fallback in a fresh session.
findings.evidence: A service worker is registered and the manifest is installable, but Cache Storage was empty; a missing route returned a bare 404 status with no status text.
findings.suggestedFix: Precache a lightweight offline shell and provide clear, retryable offline/timeout/404 states for articles and live data.

findings.summary: Consent choice architecture favors acceptance.
findings.evidence: The first layer presents a prominent ACEPTAR button and “Gestionar opciones”, but no equally direct reject-all action; the text discloses 63 partners while blocking content.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Accept all, Reject all and Manage choices with equal visual weight and make non-essential processing opt-in.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not responsive or format-efficient.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 93/100 images without dimensions, 87 without srcset, 93 legacy-format images and five oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height, responsive srcset/sizes and AVIF/WebP variants from the image CDN; prioritize only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Substantial work runs before the reader has chosen optional processing.
findings.evidence: The initial load transfers 4.07 MB across 188 requests, including 61 scripts; 134 requests are third-party and reduced-motion still runs 15 loaders.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional analytics, ads and personalization on consent; defer background work and stop non-essential animations when hidden or reduced motion is requested.

findings.summary: Third-party bytes exceed a reasonable news-page budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties transfer 2.90 MB (71% of all bytes) across 134 requests, led by tag management, advertising, video and social scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt an enforceable third-party budget, remove redundant vendors, and load video/ad stacks only near use and after consent.

findings.summary: The homepage has a high baseline heap and DOM footprint.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contains 1,321,436 nodes and 79.3 MB self size. After ten scroll cycles a separate fresh run measured 1,353,227 nodes and 81.7 MB, a modest but inconclusive increase.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial DOM/card count with content-visibility or pagination and eliminate unnecessary third-party object graphs; set heap/DOM budgets for long sessions.

taskList.title: Gate optional analytics, ads, video and personalization on purpose-specific consent; remove duplicate vendors and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.
Redesign consent and notification prompting so reading stays available and Accept all, Reject all and Manage choices have equal prominence.
Optimize the mobile LCP chain and main thread by prioritizing the lead asset, deferring non-critical scripts and breaking up long tasks.
Deploy HSTS, nosniff, explicit referrer/permissions policies and a restrictive nonce/hash-based CSP.
Emit image dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes and modern AVIF/WebP variants.
Fix unnamed interactive controls and consent-dialog text contrast.
Contain integration failures, remove deprecated/unload behavior and provide useful offline, timeout and 404 states.
Honor dark mode and reduced motion across first-party and consent/loading surfaces.
Reduce the initial DOM and heap footprint through pagination/content-visibility and third-party object-graph reduction.
Simplify opening chrome and add restrained progressive navigation/scroll continuity where it supports reading.
